iterations.note: First review of all stories (1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 7, 8, 4) against each other, DECISIONS.md and the Assignment 1 designs

findings.title: Condition is scored per version, but condition belongs to each copy (listing)

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition (illustrative data)
Listing: claimed version, actual version, price, condition, seller, city, photos

proposal.section: Story 3 · How the pick is made
proposal.current: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition (illustrative data)
proposal.proposed: Sound and original scores (1–5) are stored per version (illustrative data). The condition score is calculated: the best condition among the version's listings on sale (M = 5, NM = 4, VG+ = 3, VG = 2, G = 1).

findings.title: Price score is stored per version, while real prices live in the listings and change

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Each version has a score from 1 to 5 for each criterion: sound, price, original, condition
number of listings, lowest price

proposal.section: Story 3 · How the pick is made
proposal.proposed: The price score is calculated from each version's lowest price on sale: the cheapest version of the album scores 5, the most expensive scores 1, the others in between (rounded to the nearest whole number).

findings.title: Reasons are fixed per version, but Assignment 1 asks for reasons tied to the buyer's priorities

evidence.quote: Reason text: fixed sentences per version
One version, with reasons tied to my priorities
e.g. "Costs €32, vs €185 for a first pressing"

proposal.section: Story 3 · Data used / What the screen shows
proposal.current: Reason text: fixed sentences per version
proposal.proposed: Reason text: fixed sentences per version and per criterion (sound, price, original, condition). The screen shows the sentences for the buyer's chosen priorities, in rank order (max 3). Prices inside sentences come from the data, not from the text.

findings.title: Which listings count for a version is not defined (counts, lowest price, "No listings", "has listings")

evidence.quote: label "No listings" when the album has no active listings

evidence.where: Story 3 · How the pick is made
evidence.quote: Only versions with at least one active listing can be recommended
Red listing → appears here as a warning and also under the correct version

proposal.section: New section before Story 1 · Shared rules
proposal.proposed: Active listing: a listing on sale (not sold, not removed) that is green or yellow. Counts, lowest price, "No listings" and "has listings" use active listings only. A red listing counts for its actual version, not for the version the seller claimed.

findings.title: Album with no listings leads the buyer through the priorities screen to a dead end

evidence.quote: Album with no listings → shown, not hidden
Tapping an album opens the priorities screen (story 2)
No version of the album has listings → no recommendation; message: "Nobody is selling this album right now"

proposal.current: Tapping an album opens the priorities screen (story 2)
proposal.proposed: Tapping an album with active listings opens the priorities screen (story 2). Tapping an album with no listings shows "Nobody is selling this album right now" directly, without the priorities screen.

findings.question: Should an album with no listings skip the priorities screen and show the message straight away?

findings.title: Traffic light of a red listing once it appears under its correct version is undefined

evidence.quote: appears here as a warning and also under the correct version, where it is checked again
Check result: listing, item (cover/label, country/year, matrix), result

proposal.proposed: where it is shown yellow ("Moved here · check pending"), because its checklist was made against the claimed version, not this one.

findings.question: Under its correct version, should a moved listing show yellow until it is checked again?

findings.title: "Suggestions close to the typed text" cannot be tested: no rule for how close or how many

evidence.quote: A search with no matches shows suggestions close to the typed text ("Did you mean Ziggy Stardust?")

proposal.current: A search with no matches shows suggestions close to the typed text
proposal.proposed: A search with no matches shows up to 3 album titles that differ from the typed text by at most 2 letters (e.g. "zigy" → "Did you mean Ziggy Stardust?"). With no such album, it shows "No albums found".

findings.title: Condition grades differ between the story and the sell screen design

evidence.quote: Mint (M), Near Mint (NM), Very Good Plus (VG+), Very Good (VG), Good (G)
Near mint NM · Very good VG+ · Good VG · Fair G

findings.question: Which condition list is the one: the story's five grades (M, NM, VG+, VG, G) or the design's four (Near mint, Very good, Good, Fair)?

findings.title: After login from Buy: story 9 returns to the listing, story 7 returns to the checkout

evidence.quote: Tapping Buy while signed out opens login and, after login, returns to the same listing
Buyer not signed in → login first (story 9), then back to the checkout

proposal.section: Story 9 · Acceptance criteria and Edge cases
proposal.current: after login, returns to the same listing
proposal.proposed: after login, goes to the checkout for that listing

findings.title: Price label of a red listing: compared with which version's typical range?

evidence.quote: Every listing in the list (green, yellow and red) shows its label

proposal.proposed: A red listing is compared with the typical range of its actual version.

findings.title: Does "Change" overwrite the saved priorities of a signed-in buyer?

evidence.quote: Signed-in buyer: the ranking is saved to the account
Saved ranking but this album is different → "Change" on the recommendation

proposal.proposed: When a signed-in buyer changes the ranking, the new ranking replaces the saved one.

findings.question: When a signed-in buyer changes priorities for one album, should that become the saved ranking?

findings.title: Nothing stops a seller from buying their own listing

evidence.quote: One account for buying and selling
Buy (green and yellow only)

proposal.proposed: A signed-in seller sees their own listings without the Buy button ("Your listing").

findings.title: No story says where "My listings" is reached from

evidence.quote: "My listings": see, edit and remove own listings
Header: search, Sell for free and the account menu. On mobile, the menu is a hamburger.

proposal.proposed: "My listings" is reached from the account menu (initials on desktop, hamburger on mobile).

findings.title: Story 4 links to a "version page" that no story defines

evidence.quote: Tapping a version → its recommendation-style page with its listings

findings.question: Define the version page when phase 4 is reached (or drop the link from the comparison)?

findings.title: No story has a Pre-condition section

evidence.quote: Sections used: Scope, Use cases, Acceptance criteria, Edge cases, Data used, Non-functional, Out of scope

proposal.proposed: ### Pre-condition — e.g. Story 3: the buyer picked an album with active listings and at least one priority. Story 7: the buyer is signed in and tapped Buy on a green or yellow listing on sale.

findings.title: Loading and error states are missing (data takes time, or fails to load or save)

evidence.quote: (no loading or failure case listed)

proposal.proposed: While data loads, screens show a placeholder. If loading or saving fails, the screen says what failed and offers "Try again"; nothing typed is lost.

findings.title: "Every technical term" is not testable without a list of terms

evidence.quote: Every technical term on the screen has a plain explanation

proposal.current: Every technical term on the screen has a plain explanation
proposal.proposed: Every term in the glossary (at least: remaster, reissue, first pressing, matrix, and each condition grade) shows its plain explanation wherever it appears

findings.title: The plain-language line of each priority is only given for Price; the design has all four

evidence.quote: each with a short plain-language line (e.g. Price: "I don't want to overpay")
I want the best-sounding one · I don't want to overpay · I want the first pressing · I want a near-mint copy

proposal.proposed: Sound: "I want the best-sounding one" · Price: "I don't want to overpay" · Original: "I want the first pressing" · Condition: "I want a near-mint copy"

findings.title: Search results in the design show "from €24 · 3 verified copies"; the story moved price to the detail page without recording why

evidence.quote: Ziggy Stardust · David Bowie, 1972 · from €24 · 3 verified copies · 477 versions
Search result: cover, album title, artist, release year, number of versions

proposal.proposed:
### Search results show no price or listing count (story 1)
- Why: (your reason)

findings.question: Keep the results without price and copies (then record why), or follow the design?

findings.title: Typical price: the story shows a range (€28–€36), the design shows one value (€32); the change is not recorded

evidence.quote: Below the list: "Typical price for this pressing: €28–€36"
Typical price for this pressing: €32

proposal.proposed:
### The typical price is shown as a range, not one value (story 6)
- Why: a range explains why a price is "Typical" (the sell screen design already uses a range: €24–34).

findings.title: Listings on the same screen as the recommendation (story), but on a separate screen on mobile (design)

evidence.quote: Below it, the listings for that version (story 5)
Compare · See verified listings
3 for sale · 1 moved

proposal.current: Below it, the listings for that version (story 5)
proposal.proposed: Desktop: the listings appear beside the recommendation. Phone: a "See verified listings" button opens them on their own screen (as in the designs).

findings.title: Sign-in error text differs from the design, and the design's text mentions a password reset that is out of scope

evidence.quote: A wrong password shows "Email or password is wrong"
That email and password don't match. Check them and try again, or reset your password.
No email confirmation or password reset in the MVP

proposal.current: A wrong password shows "Email or password is wrong"
proposal.proposed: A wrong password shows "That email and password don't match. Check them and try again." (no reset link in the MVP)

findings.title: The design's sign-up has "I also want to sell records" and a terms line; the story has neither

evidence.quote: I also want to sell records (it's free) · By creating an account you accept the terms and privacy policy.
Sign up with name, email and password

findings.question: With one account for buying and selling, drop the "I also want to sell" checkbox? Keep the terms line as text only?

findings.title: Checkout design shows a saved address and a phone number for MB WAY; the story types the address each time and shows the method as a label only — not recorded in DECISIONS

evidence.quote: Ship to Rua do Almada 120, Porto · Change · Pay with MB WAY · 912 *** 345 · Change
typed for each order, not saved · choice of MB WAY or card, as a label only

proposal.proposed:
### Checkout address is typed for each order; the payment method is a label only (story 7)
- Why: no personal data stored beyond the order; payment is simulated.

findings.title: The design explains what protection covers; the story does not include that text

evidence.quote: What protection covers: Pressing check, payment held until delivery, and a refund if the record isn't as listed.

proposal.proposed: - "What protection covers: pressing check, payment held until delivery, and a refund if the record isn't as listed."

findings.title: Comparison rows: story shows 1–5 scores, design shows plain words (Cleaner / Warmer, Yes / No, Near mint / Worn)

evidence.quote: sound, price, original, condition (scores 1–5)
Sound: Cleaner / Warmer · Typical price: €32 / €185 · First pressing? No / Yes · Condition for sale: Near mint / Worn

proposal.proposed: sound (short word from the data, e.g. "Cleaner"), typical price, first pressing (Yes / No), best condition on sale (grade name), number for sale

findings.title: Is a payment method required before Pay, and is one pre-selected?

evidence.quote: Pay is disabled until the address fields are filled in
Payment method: choice of MB WAY or card, as a label only

proposal.current: choice of MB WAY or card, as a label only
proposal.proposed: choice of MB WAY or card, as a label only; MB WAY is selected by default

questions.question: Condition list: the story's five grades (M, NM, VG+, VG, G) or the design's four (Near mint, Very good, Good, Fair)?
Album with no listings: skip the priorities screen and show the message straight away?
Moved (red) listing under its correct version: yellow until checked again?
Does changing priorities replace the saved ranking?
Search results without price and copies (record why), or follow the design?
Drop the "I also want to sell records" checkbox; keep the terms line as text?
Story 4: define the version page in phase 4, or drop the link?
